notes: 0.15.1 is COMMITTED AND PUSHED BUT NOT PUBLISHED to npm -- npm latest is 0.15.0. The publish is a separate, deliberate act and it is waiting on an explicit go-ahead, not on a technical blocker. What 0.15.1 does: 0.15.0's dormancy rule is correct and unchanged, but a reserved category that had NOT armed said nothing about it. A controller declared from a bare terminal takes the cli:<user> fallback, carries no process id and arms nothing; the only way to learn that was to notice a guard that should have fired never did. A protection believed to be on and actually off is worse than no protection, because it is trusted. casp live claims now states where the reserved category stands AND WHY in every state, --json gains reserved_paths { armed, reason }, and a kill switch reports armed: false. Reporting only: no verdict changes, no new subcommand, no rule, and check still sees none of it. Docs also name the limit that matters most -- casp live guards PATH WRITES, not the side effects of shared state. Measured case: a git add of one file followed by git commit published 945 lines of unrelated staged deletions, because git commit without a pathspec publishes the whole index, one object shared by every process in the repo. No claim would have prevented it; the guard saw a Bash call and Bash is deliberately unguarded. Same family: regenerated lockfile, schema migration, dev-server port, build cache. 222 tests.
